SECURITY ADVISORY // OWASP A01:2025
Broken Access Control & SSRF
Category
OWASP A01:2025
Severity
CRITICAL (CVSS 9.1)
CWE Mapping
CWE-284, CWE-639 (IDOR), CWE-918 (SSRF)
Target Gate
NAVI GITWARE Pre-Push
1. Vulnerability Overview
Access control enforces policy such that users cannot act outside of their intended permissions. Failures typically lead to
unauthorized information disclosure, modification, or destruction of all data. In OWASP Top 10:2025, this category also absorbs
Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF).
2. Common Vulnerable Patterns in Code Diffs
• Insecure Direct Object References (IDOR): trusting user-supplied IDs in URLs or payloads without ownership checks.
• Missing function-level access control on administrative or sensitive API endpoints.
• Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF): fetching arbitrary remote URLs supplied by users without allowlisting.
3. Vulnerable Code Example (Block Condition)
# VULNERABLE: IDOR & SSRF
@app.get("/api/invoices/{invoice_id}")
def get_invoice(invoice_id: int):
    return db.query(Invoice).filter_by(id=invoice_id).first()
@app.post("/api/webhook/test")
def test_webhook(url: str):
    return requests.get(url).text
4. Secure Implementation Pattern
# SECURE: Enforce ownership & strict URL allowlist
@app.get("/api/invoices/{invoice_id}")
def get_invoice(invoice_id: int, user=Depends(current_user)):
    return db.query(Invoice).filter_by(id=invoice_id, owner_id=user.id).first()
5. Remediation Checklist
Deny access by default. Enforce record ownership checks on the server for every request, disable directory listing, and validate
external URLs against a strict domain allowlist.

SECURITY ADVISORY // OWASP A08:2025
Software & Data Integrity Failures
Category
OWASP A08:2025
Severity
CRITICAL (CVSS 9.0)
CWE Mapping
CWE-502 (Insecure Deserialization), CWE-353, CWE-494
Target Gate
NAVI GITWARE Pre-Push
1. Vulnerability Overview
Integrity failures occur when applications trust code, plugins, updates, or serialized data structures from untrusted sources without
verifying cryptographic signatures or integrity, frequently resulting in Remote Code Execution (RCE).
2. Common Vulnerable Patterns in Code Diffs
• Deserializing untrusted user payloads with Python pickle, yaml.load(), or Java ObjectInputStream.
• Loading external CDN scripts without Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes.
• Applying auto-updates or webhooks without HMAC/digital signature verification.
3. Vulnerable Code Example (Block Condition)
# VULNERABLE: Arbitrary code execution via pickle / unsafe YAML
import pickle, yaml
user_state = pickle.loads(base64.b64decode(request.cookies["state"]))
config = yaml.load(request.body, Loader=yaml.Loader)
4. Secure Implementation Pattern
# SECURE: Safe data formats (JSON / yaml.safe_load) + HMAC
import json, yaml
user_state = json.loads(verify_hmac(request.cookies["state"]))
config = yaml.safe_load(request.body)
5. Remediation Checklist
Never deserialize untrusted data with pickle or unsafe YAML loaders; use JSON with schema validation, verify webhook HMAC
signatures, and enforce SRI on external assets.

SECURITY ADVISORY // OWASP A02:2025
Security Misconfiguration
Category
OWASP A02:2025
Severity
HIGH (CVSS 8.2)
CWE Mapping
CWE-16, CWE-209, CWE-215, CWE-942
Target Gate
NAVI GITWARE Pre-Push
1. Vulnerability Overview
Security misconfiguration occurs when system, framework, cloud, or application settings are left insecure, unhardened, or overly
permissive. Climbing to #2 in OWASP Top 10:2025, it frequently exposes internal stack traces, default accounts, and public cloud
storage.
2. Common Vulnerable Patterns in Code Diffs
• Debug mode enabled in production (DEBUG=True), leaking stack traces and environment variables.
• Overly permissive CORS policies (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * with credentials).
• Unchanged default credentials, exposed admin consoles, or publicly readable S3/blob buckets.
3. Vulnerable Code Example (Block Condition)
# VULNERABLE: Production debug enabled & wildcard CORS
app = FastAPI(debug=True)
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["*"],
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
)
4. Secure Implementation Pattern
# SECURE: Environment-driven hardening & explicit origins
app = FastAPI(debug=False, docs_url=None)
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["https://app.example.com"],
    allow_credentials=True,
)
5. Remediation Checklist
Automate hardened configurations across dev, staging, and prod. Disable debug flags and verbose error pages in production, and
restrict CORS origins explicitly.

SECURITY ADVISORY // OWASP A07:2025
Authentication & Session Failures
Category
OWASP A07:2025
Severity
HIGH (CVSS 8.8)
CWE Mapping
CWE-287, CWE-384, CWE-521, CWE-613
Target Gate
NAVI GITWARE Pre-Push
1. Vulnerability Overview
Authentication failures allow attackers to compromise passwords, keys, or session tokens, or exploit implementation flaws to assume
legitimate user identities via credential stuffing, brute force, or weak JWT/session handling.
2. Common Vulnerable Patterns in Code Diffs
• Accepting JWTs without signature verification (algorithms=['none'] or decode(..., verify=False)).
• Missing brute-force protection, weak password policies, or lack of MFA on privileged accounts.
• Session tokens exposed in URLs, lacking HttpOnly/Secure flags, or not invalidated on logout.
3. Vulnerable Code Example (Block Condition)
# VULNERABLE: Unverified JWT decoding & permissive cookie
payload = jwt.decode(token, options={"verify_signature": False})
response.set_cookie("session_id", sid, httponly=False, secure=False)
4. Secure Implementation Pattern
# SECURE: Strict algorithm pinning & hardened cookie flags
payload = jwt.decode(token, PUBLIC_KEY, algorithms=["RS256"])
response.set_cookie("session_id", sid, httponly=True, secure=True, samesite="Strict")
5. Remediation Checklist
Enforce MFA, pin JWT verification algorithms explicitly, set HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite cookie attributes, rotate session IDs on login,
and throttle login attempts.

41aa085fe6d2529af97c90b39d56e57bc6df1a7e.report_text:
SECURITY ADVISORY // OWASP A10:2025
Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions
Category
OWASP A10:2025
Severity
HIGH (CVSS 7.5)
CWE Mapping
CWE-755, CWE-636 (Fail Open), CWE-460, CWE-248
Target Gate
NAVI GITWARE Pre-Push
1. Vulnerability Overview
Introduced in OWASP Top 10:2025, this category covers improper error handling, failing open during exceptions, missing transaction
rollbacks, and resource leaks that leave applications in exploitable or corrupted states.
2. Common Vulnerable Patterns in Code Diffs
• Failing open: granting access or bypassing security checks when an auth/policy service throws an exception.
• Partial multi-step financial or state mutations without atomic database transaction rollbacks.
• Bare except blocks hiding critical security exceptions or leaving file/socket handles open.
3. Vulnerable Code Example (Block Condition)
# VULNERABLE: Fail-open authorization & non-atomic transfer
def is_authorized(user, resource):
    try:
        return policy_engine.check(user, resource)
    except Exception:
        return True  # Fails open on timeout/error!
4. Secure Implementation Pattern
# SECURE: Fail-closed authorization & explicit error logging
def is_authorized(user, resource):
    try:
        return policy_engine.check(user, resource)
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.error("Policy engine failure, denying access", exc_info=exc)
        return False
5. Remediation Checklist
Always fail closed on security and authorization errors, wrap multi-step state mutations in atomic transactions with rollback, and use
centralized exception handlers.

SECURITY ADVISORY // OWASP A05:2025
Injection (SQLi, Command & XSS)
Category
OWASP A05:2025
Severity
CRITICAL (CVSS 9.8)
CWE Mapping
CWE-89 (SQLi), CWE-78 (OS CMDi), CWE-79 (XSS)Target Gate
NAVI GITWARE Pre-Push
1. Vulnerability Overview
Injection flaws occur when untrusted user-supplied data is concatenated directly into an interpreter command or query without
parameterization or context-aware escaping, enabling arbitrary SQL execution, OS command execution, or Cross-Site Scripting.
2. Common Vulnerable Patterns in Code Diffs
• String formatting or f-strings used to build SQL queries with user input.
• Passing unsanitized user parameters to subprocess with shell=True or os.system().
• Rendering raw unescaped HTML in templates (|safe, dangerouslySetInnerHTML).
3. Vulnerable Code Example (Block Condition)
# VULNERABLE: SQL Injection & OS Command Injection
cursor.execute(f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '{user_email}'")
subprocess.run(f"ping -c 1 {host}", shell=True)
4. Secure Implementation Pattern
# SECURE: Parameterized SQL & argument array without shell
cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = %s", (user_email,))
subprocess.run(["ping", "-c", "1", host], shell=False, check=True)
5. Remediation Checklist
Always use parameterized queries or ORM bindings, avoid shell=True in subprocess calls, validate inputs against strict allowlists,
and apply context-aware output encoding.

SECURITY ADVISORY // OWASP A09:2025
Security Logging & Alerting Failures
Category
OWASP A09:2025
Severity
MEDIUM (CVSS 6.5)
CWE Mapping
CWE-778, CWE-117 (Log Injection), CWE-532
Target Gate
NAVI GITWARE Pre-Push
1. Vulnerability Overview
Insufficient logging, monitoring, and alerting prevent organizations from detecting active breaches in time. Conversely, improper
logging can introduce Log Injection or leak sensitive credentials and tokens into plaintext log files.
2. Common Vulnerable Patterns in Code Diffs
• Swallowing authentication failures or access-control denials without structured audit logs.
• Logging raw passwords, authorization headers, or PII tokens in application logs.
• Writing unsanitized user input directly into log lines (CRLF log forging).
3. Vulnerable Code Example (Block Condition)
# VULNERABLE: Logging raw credentials & swallowing auth failures
try:
    authenticate(user, password)
except AuthError:
    pass  # Silent failure, no audit trail
logger.info(f"Login attempt: user={user}, password={password}, headers={req.headers}")
4. Secure Implementation Pattern
# SECURE: Structured audit event without secrets
try:
    authenticate(user, password)
except AuthError:
    audit_log.warning("auth_failed", extra={"user": sanitize(user), "ip": req.client.host})
    raise
5. Remediation Checklist
Log all authentication, access-control, and input-validation failures with structured context; redact secrets/tokens; sanitize newlines;
and configure real-time alerts.

SECURITY ADVISORY // OWASP A06:2025
Insecure Design
Category
OWASP A06:2025
Severity
HIGH (CVSS 7.8)
CWE Mapping
CWE-209, CWE-256, CWE-501, CWE-799
Target Gate
NAVI GITWARE Pre-Push
1. Vulnerability Overview
Insecure design represents architectural and business-logic flaws where security controls were never conceived during planning.
Even a bug-free implementation cannot compensate for missing rate limits, trust boundary violations, or abusable workflows.
2. Common Vulnerable Patterns in Code Diffs
• Missing rate limiting or anti-automation controls on OTP, password reset, or payment endpoints.
• Relying on client-side hidden fields or prices for e-commerce checkout calculations.
• Unlimited resource allocation (file uploads, batch queries) enabling Denial of Service.
3. Vulnerable Code Example (Block Condition)
# VULNERABLE: Trusting client-supplied price & no rate limit
@app.post("/api/checkout")
def checkout(items: list[dict], total_price: float):
    charge_card(user.card, amount=total_price)
    return {"status": "paid"}
4. Secure Implementation Pattern
# SECURE: Server-side price calculation & rate limiting
@app.post("/api/checkout")
@limiter.limit("5/minute")
def checkout(item_ids: list[int]):
    total = calculate_server_total(item_ids)
    charge_card(user.card, amount=total)
5. Remediation Checklist
Integrate threat modeling early in SDLC, enforce server-side business invariants, apply strict rate limiting and quotas, and segregate
trust tiers.

SECURITY ADVISORY // OWASP A04:2025
Cryptographic Failures
Category
OWASP A04:2025
Severity
HIGH (CVSS 8.6)
CWE Mapping
CWE-327, CWE-328, CWE-798, CWE-319
Target Gate
NAVI GITWARE Pre-Push
1. Vulnerability Overview
Cryptographic failures expose sensitive data (credentials, PII, tokens) due to missing encryption, deprecated algorithms (MD5,
SHA-1, DES, ECB mode), weak random number generation, or hardcoded cryptographic keys in source code.
2. Common Vulnerable Patterns in Code Diffs
• Hashing passwords with fast, broken algorithms like MD5 or SHA-1 without salt.
• Hardcoding API keys, JWT secrets, or encryption keys directly in repositories.
• Disabling TLS certificate verification (verify=False) or transmitting data over HTTP.
3. Vulnerable Code Example (Block Condition)
# VULNERABLE: Hardcoded secret, MD5 hashing & disabled TLS check
JWT_SECRET = "super_secret_static_key_123"
pwd_hash = hashlib.md5(password.encode()).hexdigest()
resp = requests.post("https://partner.api/auth", json=data, verify=False)
4. Secure Implementation Pattern
# SECURE: Env secret, Argon2id/bcrypt & strict TLS
JWT_SECRET = os.environ["JWT_SECRET"]
pwd_hash = password_hasher.hash(password)  # Argon2id
resp = requests.post("https://partner.api/auth", json=data, verify=True)
5. Remediation Checklist
Use Argon2id or bcrypt for passwords, AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 for data at rest, enforce TLS 1.3 with certificate
validation, and load secrets from a vault.

SECURITY ADVISORY // OWASP A03:2025
Software Supply Chain Failures
Category
OWASP A03:2025
Severity
CRITICAL (CVSS 9.4)
CWE Mapping
CWE-1104, CWE-829, CWE-494
Target Gate
NAVI GITWARE Pre-Push
1. Vulnerability Overview
Expanded in OWASP Top 10:2025, this category covers compromises across third-party dependencies, build pipelines, CI/CD
runners, and distribution channels. Attackers exploit unpinned packages, typosquatting, or known CVEs in transitive libraries.
2. Common Vulnerable Patterns in Code Diffs
• Unpinned dependencies or floating version ranges in requirements.txt / package.json.
• Pulling remote install scripts or unverified container images (:latest) without hash verification.
• Exposing secrets or excessive permissions in CI/CD workflow definitions.
3. Vulnerable Code Example (Block Condition)
# VULNERABLE: Unpinned packages & mutable base image
# requirements.txt
requests>=2.0
pyyaml
# Dockerfile
FROM python:latest
RUN curl -sSL https://get.vendor.io/install.sh | bash
4. Secure Implementation Pattern
# SECURE: Exact versions, hashes & pinned image digest
# requirements.txt
requests==2.32.3 --hash=sha256:70761cfe03c773ceb22aa2f671b4757976145175cdfca038c02654d061d6dcc6
# Dockerfile
FROM python:3.12.7-slim@sha256:9f8b...
5. Remediation Checklist
Maintain an SBOM, lock exact dependency versions with cryptographic hashes, pin container images by SHA-256 digest, and run
automated SCA scans in CI.
